name: Muse Spark 1.3 Free
feedback: Build the Cozy Haven Room around a focal triangle—woven rug, monstera, and wicker basket—with an oat-dominant backdrop, asymmetrical prop layering, and translucent amber sunbeams that feel suspended in dust rather than pasted onto the scene. Give all nine pets consistent silhouette weight and simplified geometry, but vary ear, tail, body, and marking shapes for thumbnail readability; use double catchlights selectively on eyes and upper-facing surfaces, avoiding equal gloss across every variant. Anchor each character with a soft fern-caramel contact shadow that widens and fades as elevation increases, balancing the “floating” fantasy with believable weight. Use the palette near 60% oat, 25% fern, 10% caramel, and 5% amber, adding darker outline values if oat-on-oat details lose contrast.

name: MiMo-V2.6 Flash Free
feedback:
At cozy zoom, make window dust feel atmospheric rather than snowy: use 1–3 px soft motes at α 0.12–0.25, drifting diagonally at 2–8 px/s with gentle curl, mostly behind characters but with a few foreground motes for depth.  
For petting and feeding, use 6–12 px hearts at α 0.7–0.9 bursting upward/outward at 25–60 px/s, while 2–5 px crumb flecks at α 0.8–1.0 fall in lively 30–90 px/s arcs—layer both above the interaction point but below the UI.  
Dream bubbles should be translucent 8–18 px shapes at α 0.25–0.45, rising at 4–12 px/s with soft lateral sway, whereas minigame sparkles should stay tiny at 2–6 px and α 0.35–0.7, floating at 3–10 px/s.  
Keep textures feathered, use normal blending for dust and hearts, additive blending only for sparkles, and avoid dense emissions so every effect remains gentle and readable.

name: Big Pickle
feedback: The Baking UI will feel warmer and more authentic with appetizing illustrated sprites: bubbling Pho Bo with delicate steam curls, golden-crusted Banh Mi scoring, and creamy Ca Phe Trung swirls. Replace raw completion text such as “OK 5/1” with mint-green checkmark pills for a cleaner, friendlier hierarchy. Style the Bake button in warm apricot with subtle highlights and a gently pressed state to make it inviting. On completion, add a celebratory starburst glow behind the dish, paired with tiny sparkles that emphasize freshness and achievement.

name: Step-5 Preview Free
feedback: The Gathering Walk already feels like a gentle meadow, but depth will improve with pale, wet washes and low-contrast silhouettes in the distance, transitioning to warmer, denser forms in the foreground. Use layered translucent washes of lavender, sage, butter yellow, and muted coral, allowing controlled pigment blooms and softened contours to create watercolor color bleeding without muddying the path. Establish three clear planes: tall grass and collectibles in front, clustered wildflowers and leafy bushes in the middle, and faint butterflies and horizon shapes behind. Scatter flowers and bushes in organic drifts, nestle collectibles into tall grass with a subtle glint or petal cue, and give butterflies varied looping flight paths so the environment feels alive while keeping interactables readable.

name: Fledge Alpha Free
feedback:
1. **Hierarchy:** Treat the critter as the primary focal layer and reserve a top UI safe zone above its face and eyes, keeping toasts and tooltips visually above both.  
2. **Toast layout:** Stack banners vertically with consistent padding and timing; anchor object notifications to the relevant edge with an 8–12 px offset and short leader line, then clamp them within the viewport.  
3. **Placement preview:** Preserve the decoration’s full silhouette with a soft ground shadow—tinted green and check-marked when valid, muted red and warning-marked when invalid—rather than relying on transparency alone.  
4. **Small screens:** Use at least 14–16 px text, solid high-contrast badges with a 4.5:1 text-contrast ratio, redundant icons/labels instead of color-only cues, and reposition critical badges away from the critter rather than shrinking them.
